title: Network Foundations
description: Inspect the switch to understand frames, MAC addresses, and how the switch learns.
scenario: Inspect the switch to understand frames, MAC addresses, and how the switch learns.

concepts.title: Frames & Packets
concepts.body: Data travels as frames (Layer 2) inside packets (Layer 3). Frames carry MAC addresses; packets carry IP addresses.
concepts.code:
Frame: [MAC src][MAC dst][Packet]
Packet: [IP src][IP dst][Data]

concepts.title: MAC Addresses
concepts.body: Every NIC has a unique 48-bit MAC address like 00:1B:2F:3C:4D:5E. Switches use MACs to forward frames to the right port.

concepts.title: How Switches Learn
concepts.body: A switch learns MAC addresses by reading the source MAC of every frame. It builds a MAC address table mapping MAC → port.
concepts.code:
Switch# show mac address-table
MAC Address    Port
00:1B:2F:3C:4D:5E  Fa0/1
00:1B:2F:3C:4D:5F  Fa0/2

concepts.title: Broadcast Behavior
concepts.body: If the switch does not know a destination MAC, it floods the frame out all ports (except the source). This is how ARP works.
concepts.code: Unknown MAC → flood to all ports
